title: Compress a complete writing process
instructions: Use this fictional practice record. Run 1 used a fresh reflective prompt and a 45-minute clock: Nara used a prompt checklist and full planning frame, finished a complete response in 43 minutes and began a meaning-first check with five minutes remaining. Run 2 used a fresh comparable prompt and a 35-minute clock: Nara used only a compact task–focus–paragraph-route note and neutral time signals, finished in 34 minutes and began checking with four minutes remaining; the opening repeated the prompt and the second reason needed fuller explanation. No person or tool supplied ideas, sentences or corrections. Nara has not yet attempted the 30-minute independent run. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which rehearsal sequence best represents safe process compression?

options.text: Repeat one memorised response at 30 minutes until its copying speed improves, then infer readiness for every prompt.

Use a supported 45-minute fresh response to locate bottlenecks, fade support on a fresh 35-minute response, then attempt a fresh 30-minute response independently when the shorter process remains complete.
Move directly to 30 minutes and remove planning, development and checking at the same time.
Keep every rehearsal at 45 minutes because timing evidence can never inform practice.

choice_rationales.A: A repeated response confounds memory with transfer and does not test the process on an unseen task.
choice_rationales.B: The sequence reduces time and support in bounded stages while requiring the complete process to transfer to fresh prompts.
choice_rationales.C: Changing every condition at once removes the safeguards and makes the cause of failure unclear.
choice_rationales.D: Supported practice is useful, but the lesson outcome requires a controlled move toward the reported independent limit.

parts.hint: Choose the sequence that changes time and support gradually while testing each stage on fresh material.
parts.correct_explanation: Bounded compression uses one stage to diagnose, the next to fade support and a fresh independent run to test transfer.

parts.prompt: Which THREE details from the record are relevant when deciding what Nara should practise before the 30-minute run?

options.text: Both rehearsals reached a complete ending within their clocks.
The 35-minute run preserved a four-minute checking period with reduced support.
The 35-minute response repeated its opening and underdeveloped the second reason.
Nara wrote exactly the same number of words in both responses.
One sentence in the 45-minute response used an uncommon adjective.

choice_rationales.A: Completion shows that compression has not yet removed the response's ending.
choice_rationales.B: A protected checking buffer and reduced support are direct evidence about the shorter process.
choice_rationales.C: The repetition and thin explanation identify the next bounded development repair.
choice_rationales.D: The record gives no exact word counts, and matching totals would not by itself establish quality or independence.
choice_rationales.E: One unusual word does not diagnose whether the complete process is transferring under less time.

parts.hint: Select evidence about completion, independent process and the specific quality bottleneck.
parts.correct_explanation: A compression decision should use process evidence and the largest remaining quality loss, not decorative or invented measurements.

parts.prompt: Which adjustment best targets the 35-minute bottleneck without discarding a necessary process step?

options.text: Remove the compact plan and use its time to copy the prompt into a longer introduction.
Use the entire checking buffer to add a third reason, whether or not it supports the focus.
Limit the opening to the task and controlling focus, keep the compact route, and use the saved drafting time to complete the claim–detail–explanation chain for the second reason.
Ask an adult to draft the second reason before the timer starts.

choice_rationales.A: This enlarges the recorded repetition and removes the route that protects coherence.
choice_rationales.B: A new reason does not repair the underdeveloped one and sacrifices the final check.
choice_rationales.C: The adjustment removes repeated material while preserving planning, development and checking.
choice_rationales.D: Supplied content would contaminate the learner's independent writing evidence.

parts.hint: Change the repeated opening and thin explanation, not the safeguards that kept the response complete.
parts.correct_explanation: Effective compression removes low-value repetition and redirects time to the specific missing reasoning link.

parts.prompt: Which setup would make Nara's future 30-minute run valid independent practice?

options.text: Reuse the 35-minute prompt with its response visible and ask a parent to improve sentences during the run.
Use a fresh comparable prompt, a separately controlled 30-minute clock and no hints, model answer, external editing or feedback until submission.
Begin with 30 minutes but borrow extra time from Section 1 whenever the conclusion is unfinished.
Pause the clock whenever Nara wants to search for a stronger example online.

choice_rationales.A: Visible prior writing and live editing test recall and assistance rather than independent transfer.
choice_rationales.B: Fresh material, the separate boundary and delayed feedback preserve the intended evidence.
choice_rationales.C: Borrowing time changes the reported separate composition limit.
choice_rationales.D: Unrecorded pauses and external searching change both timing and independence.

parts.hint: Preserve fresh material, the separate clock and no-help conditions.
parts.correct_explanation: An independent rehearsal is interpretable only when its task, time boundary and support conditions are controlled.

parts.prompt: Eight minutes remain in the 30-minute run. Nara has a clear focus and two developed body paragraphs, but no conclusion or checking yet. What is the safest recovery?

options.text: Start an unrelated third reason so the response becomes longer.
Rewrite the opening repeatedly until it sounds more dramatic, even if the response ends mid-sentence.
Finish the planned route with a bounded conclusion, then check task fulfilment and paragraph order before using remaining time on sentence boundaries and high-risk conventions.
Stop immediately and leave the final eight minutes unused because the original schedule changed.

choice_rationales.A: An unnecessary new reason risks both relevance and completion.
choice_rationales.B: Opening polish cannot outrank a complete ending and whole-response checking.
choice_rationales.C: This protects completion and checks the highest-impact meaning decisions before surface errors.
choice_rationales.D: A time signal should trigger the next priority, not end useful work early.

parts.hint: Protect the complete route first, then check meaning before surface polish.
parts.correct_explanation: A safe recovery stops expansion, completes the response and spends the remaining buffer in impact order.

parts.prompt: Suppose Nara's first 30-minute response is unfinished and received one mid-draft hint. Which conclusion and next step are most defensible?

options.text: The run proves Nara cannot succeed in the scholarship selection process.
The run does not yet show independent 30-minute completion; return to 35 minutes, target the recorded bottleneck and use another fresh comparable prompt before retrying independently.
Count the hinted response as independent because it used a 30-minute clock.
Repeat the identical prompt until it is memorised, then treat the faster result as proof of transfer.

choice_rationales.A: One formative rehearsal is not an official score or an admission prediction.
choice_rationales.B: The conclusion states the actual evidence limit and returns to a bounded repair stage with fresh material.
choice_rationales.C: The hint changes the independence condition, while the unfinished response changes the completion evidence.
choice_rationales.D: Faster repetition may reflect memory and cannot establish transfer to an unseen prompt.

parts.hint: State only what the run shows, repair one bottleneck and require fresh evidence before advancing.
parts.correct_explanation: An incomplete or supported run sends the learner back one stage; it does not justify a high-stakes judgement or a false transfer claim.
